blocks.text: Infections of the central nervous system can be caused by almost any infectious agent: viruses, bacteria, fungi, protozoa and flatworms.

blocks.caption: Meningitis: inflammation of the meninges due to infection
rows: bacterial meningitis is the most severe and life-threatening; viral is usually less severe; fungal is rare, mostly in people with weak immunity; parasites can also cause it
stiff neck, headache, fever; in severe cases paralysis or coma
bacterial: immediate antibiotics; viral: usually clears by itself, sometimes antivirals; fungal: long-term antifungal medicines
vaccines exist against some kinds of bacterial meningitis

blocks.prompt: Why is bacterial meningitis treated immediately while viral meningitis often is not?
blocks.explanation: Bacterial meningitis is the most severe and can kill, and antibiotics act on bacteria; viral meningitis is usually milder and self-limiting.

items: CNS infections: any agent. Meningitis: infected meninges; stiff neck, headache, fever; antibiotics for bacterial, vaccines for some.
